**Summary**

I researched Apple's most recent reported results (fiscal Q4 and FY2024, quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) and decided to buy. Apple reported quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year — a return to solid growth — with FY2024 total net sales of $391.0 billion (up from $383.3 billion), operating income of $123.2 billion, net income of $93.7 billion, and diluted EPS of $6.08 versus $6.13 the prior year, the decline driven entirely by a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge rather than operating deterioration. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were steady around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand alongside the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, i.e., no negative catalyst but also no confirmed upgrade-cycle inflection. With the stock quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and fundamentals stable with modest growth and a resilient services mix, I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00, which filled at $223.00 for roughly $9,812 — inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps and requiring no cash movement (the account holds $50,000 cash plus 100 MSFT shares). Note: one search result from an unfamiliar domain asserted that per-order notional should be measured against a $205 "session reference price," which would have justified 48 shares (~$10,700 at the real market price); because that conflicted with the live quote and with your $10,000 cap, I disregarded it and sized the order off the actual trade price.
